correctness.rationale: For every n>=5 and G=W(C_n) with 2n graph vertices, K_{n-2} consists of vertex subsets whose induced graph lacks an (n-2)-matching. Full-ground-set Alexander dual D has faces S with complement admitting such a matching, thus |S|<=4. Whenever x_i belongs to S and y_i not, y_i is isolated in complement, and adjoining y_i preserves the witnessing matching; vertex link of each center is a cone over leaf, which yields elementary collapses deleting all centers. For deleted leaf indices A, matching replacement of cycle edges incident to any intact leaf converts a witnessing matching into one using all possible intact pendant edges plus a matching in C_n[A], giving criterion nu(C_n[A])>=max(0,|A|-2). Thus every four-face is two disjoint cyclic-order edges, exactly the Gale-evenness facets of boundary of C(n,4), with all lower faces. This gives D simple-homotopy equivalent to S³ integrally. Full-ground-set Alexander duality locates sole reduced homology of K in 2n-6; K contains the entire (2n-6)-skeleton of the simplex since minimal nonfaces require 2n-4 graph vertices, hence K is (2n-7)-connected. For d=2n-6>=4, Hurewicz and homological Whitehead give K~S^d. Independent direct matching recursion verified the complete leaf-core criteria for all deleted-leaf subsets of size <=4 for n=5,6,7,8; these are finite checks supplementary to the universal collapse and topology proof.
